role.name: standards_prosecutor
role.mandate: Adversarially cross-examine every sealed pass and veto, reproduce technical claims against the exact frozen bytes where possible, test the strongest rebuttal, distinguish defect classes, and preserve the deterministic adjudication without changing any vote.
role.authorityLimit: This record adds no eighth vote. It cannot acquit the artifact, grant diagnostic or product clearance, alter a frozen source or review record, or rewrite durable history.

reviewedArtifact.byteReviewMethod: Every declared artifact hash was recomputed from Git object bytes at artifactCommit. The nine semantic working copies were also hashed and matched the frozen bytes before executable probes. Custom runtime probes loaded the hash-matched TypeScript through Vite or compiled Git-materialized bytes in an operating-system temporary directory that was removed on completion.

cleanReviewAttestation.assessment: The seven first-pass rulings are internally consistent, hash-bound to the same nine-file semantic allowlist, and attest that excluded history was not encountered. sealedRecord.prosecutorTreatment: Preserved exactly. Vetoes are not averaged against passes, and no dissent is converted into an extra vote.

frozenCountMetadataDefect.cause: The frozen generator maps profile.manifest.familyId, but familyId is a top-level profile field. Every mapped value is therefore undefined and the Set size is one.
frozenCountMetadataDefect.effect: This is a false count inside a correctly hashed manifest. It does not make the source a one-family fixture, change a sealed vote, or invalidate the independently observed four-family test result. It does show that the council verifier does not validate this declared count and that protocol metadata is not wholly self-checking.

frozenCouncilVerifier.interpretation: The verifier confirms integrity and deterministic blocked adjudication. Its pass is not substantive artifact clearance and it does not detect the matchedFamilies count error.

directInternalGate.interpretation: The declared regression suite passes. The prosecutor's accepted attacks show that its finite adversarial set is incomplete, not that these passing counts are fabricated.

A second harness materialized the same three source files directly from artifactCommit, compiled them with the declared Node and TypeScript versions, executed the attacks, and deleted its temporary directory. Question defects were inspected from the hash-matched frozen question pack.

if(sha!=='47ea4ddbb4b5d92175997be9ff4ad3d6492018208d92e393acfb9eef9fb1b48d') throw new Error('frozen hash mismatch'); const s=await createServer({configFile:false,root:process.cwd(),server:{middlewareMode:true},logLevel:'silent'}); const c=await s.ssrLoadModule('/'+path); const ps=c.G21_INTERNAL_RANGE_CANARY; const xs=c.buildG21InternalBlindInputs('G21-INTERNAL-RANGE-RUN-005-PROSECUTOR'); const map=new Map(ps.map(p=>[p.manifest.profileId,p])); const x=structuredClone(xs.find(i=>i.profileId==='RANGE-INTERNAL-CARE-I1'&&i.runtimeState==='initial')); const clean=c.buildG21CurrentClaimView(x.internalEvidence); x.currentClaims[0].kind='fabricated'; x.currentClaims[0].subjectScope='real_person'; x.currentClaims[0].audience='public'; const noHook=c.validateG21InternalBlindInput(x); x.currentClaims.toJSON=()=>clean; const safety=[c.validateG21InternalBlindInput(x),c.validateG21CanonicalInternalBlindInput(x,map.get(x.profileId))]; let accepted=0; for(const p of ps){const y=structuredClone(xs.find(i=>i.profileId===p.manifest.profileId&&i.runtimeState==='corrected')); const ids=new Set(p.internalEvidence.map(r=>r.evidenceId)); y.internalEvidence=y.internalEvidence.filter(r=>ids.has(r.evidenceId)); y.audienceAuthorities=y.audienceAuthorities.filter(a=>ids.has(a.evidenceId)); y.runtimeState='initial'; y.caseId=y.profileId+'-INITIAL'; y.currentClaims=c.buildG21CurrentClaimView(y.internalEvidence); if(c.validateG21InternalBlindInput(y).length===0&&c.validateG21CanonicalInternalBlindInput(y,p).length===0) accepted++; } const sp=map.get('RANGE-INTERNAL-STORY-I3'); const si=xs.find(i=>i.profileId===sp.manifest.profileId&&i.runtimeState==='initial'); const sr=si.internalEvidence.find(r=>r.evidenceId==='INT-STORY-007'); console.log(JSON.stringify({sha,noHook,safety,downgradeAccepted:accepted,causalBaseline:{kind:sr.claims[0].kind,text:sr.claims[0].text,runtime:c.validateG21InternalBlindInput(si),canonical:c.validateG21CanonicalInternalBlindInput(si,sp)}})); crossExamination.method: For every sealed ruling, state the strongest evidence-backed rebuttal, try to make it win, then say whether the owned ruling survives and at what scope. A surviving veto is never neutralized by a pass on another criterion.

crossVetoSynthesis.finding: Both expose missing independent authority, but at different layers. Epistemic integrity concerns who may issue semantic standing and whether fixture meaning is justified. Living Brain integrity concerns which lifecycle snapshot is current. One external trust-root design may repair both, but neither veto subsumes the other.

The toJSON bypass is an object-validation flaw, while the causal baseline is a trusted-fixture meaning flaw. Exact enums and plain-data canonicalization will not independently justify causation, and an independent semantic receipt will not by itself neutralize hostile object hooks.

The usefulness judge found one answer that cannot actually reshape its named route. The comprehension judge passed that question but found four different visible-answer defects. This is not a score conflict. Usefulness asks whether a valid answer changes the material route; comprehension asks whether a person can understand and supply the demanded answer. Both vetoes stand independently.

Formal human ownership survives. It does not make the evidence true, the input safe, the answer useful, the state current, or the words comprehensible. A human final call made from a corrupted or cryptic frame remains human-owned but not cleared.

The Reality pass accurately reports the attacks it ran, but it generalizes beyond them. Its state-relabel test changed the label without coherently changing the evidence subset. The Brain attack changes all candidate-controlled fields consistently and passes. Its malformed suite covers finite JSON samples, getters, proxies, cycles, and sparse arrays, but not an array toJSON view split. The passing counts and accepted new attacks can therefore both be true.

usefulnessVersusComprehension.apparentTension: The comprehension ruling calls STORY-I1 an explicit write-in and passes it, while the usefulness ruling vetoes its placeholder answer. Elsewhere both adult screens pass three of the comprehension judge's four challenged questions.
usefulnessVersusComprehension.resolution: The frozen contract has an option string but no write-in value field and makes notes optional. The usefulness veto therefore wins on the concrete consequence defect. Adult ease of paraphrase is relevant rebuttal evidence for ordinary wording, but it cannot supply an omitted option, missing target reference, or absent role value. The comprehension veto is retained but narrowed to the mechanically strongest defects rather than expanded by reader disagreement.

brainIntegrityVersusBehaviouralReality.apparentTension: Reality says state bindings and lifecycle roles defeat relabelled states, while Brain proves a corrected input can become an accepted initial input.
brainIntegrityVersusBehaviouralReality.resolution: The Reality regression proves only that mismatched labels and evidence are rejected. The Brain attack constructs a fully self-consistent older state using candidate-controlled state, caseId, evidence, authorities, and currentClaims. Because no independent expected-current-state value exists, both validators accept all 12 downgrades. The Reality pass remains valid for its exact finite checks but cannot support its broader all-shortcuts conclusion.

The exact R1 task and authority object still permit framing only, forbid recommendation, execution, durable-truth promotion, and named-employee assessment, and reserve the final call to a human. None of the reproduced attacks changes those capabilities.

overallConclusion.vetoOverlap: Epistemic and Brain vetoes share an independent-authority weakness but remain distinct. Usefulness and Comprehension overlap at visible answer contracts but fail different predicates. Safety is an independent hostile-object validation flaw.
overallConclusion.passDisposition: Human Agency survives at its exact capability scope. Behavioural and Implementation Reality survives only for its directly reproduced subclaims and cannot clear arbitrary input or lifecycle state admission.
overallConclusion.reason: The exact frozen baseline contains an unsupported causal fixture accepted as observation; both validators accept the toJSON live-view split; STORY-I1 accepts an unnamed placeholder as a complete route-changing answer; both validators accept coherent lifecycle downgrades for all 12 profiles; and at least RESEARCH-I1 plus FORGE-I3 retain concrete visible-answer defects. Any one valid veto blocks. Five stand.
